short: Five weeks in which Poland was overrun from two directions and the war began.
full:
German forces crossed the Polish frontier before dawn on 1 September 1939, preceded by air attacks on airfields and rail junctions and by a staged incident at the Gleiwitz radio station. The Polish army, mobilised late under Anglo-French pressure and deployed well forward to cover the industrial west, was outflanked by concentrated armour and outmatched in the air. Britain and France declared war on 3 September and did almost nothing on the Rhine frontier.

Warsaw was besieged and bombed and surrendered on 27 September. The Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September under the terms of the pact, and the last regular Polish formation gave up at Kock on 6 October. Poland was partitioned, and both occupiers set about destroying its educated class: the NKVD shot some 22,000 officers and officials at Katyn and elsewhere in the spring of 1940. Polish army and air force units reconstituted abroad and fought for the rest of the war, from the Battle of Britain to Monte Cassino.
